core_operating_system_directories.description: The primary installation folder for Windows 11 containing the central binaries, settings, and native tools.
The critical subsystem repository housing 64-bit kernel files, essential device drivers, and system .dll libraries.
The emulation layer folder allowing legacy 32-bit software and processes to run securely on 64-bit Windows 11.
The Component Store, which caches multiple versions of system modifications, handling features on demand and Windows Update rollbacks.

modern_and_classic_application_directori.description: The standard directory where native 64-bit applications place their primary components and binaries.
The default installation fallback path dedicated exclusively to 32-bit traditional desktop programs.
A highly secured, hidden folder storing Modern Universal Windows Platform (UWP) apps and native Windows 11 features like the redesigned Start Menu and Taskbar packages.
A hidden global folder used by applications to cache configuration properties, updates, and data shared among all local users.

profile_and_local_configuration_director.description: The structural root for all user accounts, protecting unique documents, layouts, and system configurations.
A hidden user folder containing isolated application contexts divided into Local, LocalLow, and Roaming structures.

critical_storage_and_repair_directories.description: A restricted folder managing volume metadata, security descriptors, search indexes, and System Restore points.
Holds the local recovery environment tools used to launch automatic repairs if Windows 11 fails to boot.
The system directory that temporarily caches discarded files for every storage partition before deletion.
